root_cause: When pubkey_pem_to_der() was converted from a fixed malloc'd buffer (which was always allocated to at least 1 byte, guaranteeing a valid, if empty, C string) to a lazily-allocated dynbuf (struct dynbuf), the code failed to account for the case where zero bytes are ever appended to the dynbuf. In that case Curl_dyn_ptr()/curlx_dyn_ptr() legitimately returns NULL (mirroring the dynbuf's internal unallocated state), but the caller did not check for this before handing the pointer to the base64 decoder.
findings: pubkey_pem_to_der() strips newlines/CRs from the base64 body found between the '-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----' and '-----END PUBLIC KEY-----' markers by appending each non-newline character into a dynbuf (pbuf) via Curl_dyn_addn().
